name: Cognizant

roles.name: GenC (Programmer Analyst Trainee)
roles.note: Base track. Secondary sources say all candidates are first evaluated for GenC. Cognizant's official GenC page describes the program as its hiring and development program for emerging talent in India.

roles.name: GenC Next
roles.note: Higher track requiring coding. Secondary sources cite ~₹6.75 LPA from earlier campus material; no verified 2026 CTC found.

roles.name: GenC Pro
roles.note: Mid/upper track named in 2026 campus material per secondary sources; detailed round structure not confirmed.

rounds.name: Communication Assessment
rounds.what_they_check: Spoken English through reading and repeat-sentence style tasks (per placementpreparation.io). Timings reported by sources are inconsistent.
prep: Practise reading short passages aloud clearly.
Practise listen-and-repeat drills for sentence accuracy.
Test your microphone and take it in a quiet room.

rounds.name: Aptitude Assessment (Quant, Verbal, Reasoning)
rounds.what_they_check: Quant, English and logical reasoning; reported as an elimination round with sectional cutoffs. The 25/20/35 split in 100 minutes is from a GenC Next pattern on placementpreparation.io; FACE Prep describes shorter GenC formats (e.g. ~55 questions in 60 minutes), so expect variation.
prep: Do not neglect English: candidate reports say the verbal sectional cutoff is where many fail.
Practise arithmetic (percentages, profit & loss, time & work) and number series.
Practise logical puzzles, blood relations and direction sense under time pressure.

rounds.name: Coding Assessment (GenC Next / GenC Pro)
rounds.what_they_check: Problem-solving in a language of your choice. Sources conflict on format (e.g. 2 problems in 45 minutes vs 4 problems in 120 minutes), so counts and time are unknown. Older material mentions 'Automata Fix' style debugging.
prep: Practise easy–medium array, string and math problems.
Practise fixing buggy code snippets (debugging-style questions).
Get comfortable with one language's input/output and standard collections.

rounds.name: Technical + HR Interview
rounds.what_they_check: Basics of programming, DBMS and your projects, plus flexibility on location and shifts. Secondary sources describe a combined technical and HR discussion; GenC Next/Pro interviews go deeper.
prep: Explain your project end to end, including what you would improve.
Revise OOP, SQL queries and one language's fundamentals.
Prepare honest answers on relocation, shifts and why Cognizant.

cutoffs.note: Not published; Cognizant does not release cutoffs. Secondary sources agree sectional cutoffs apply (a very low score in any section is reported to be a reject) and give candidate-reported targets in correct-answer counts rather than percentages, so no single percentage is given.

cse_it.note: Aim for GenC Next/Pro, which require the coding assessment.

ece_eee.note: Generally eligible for B.E/B.Tech tracks (confirm in your drive notice). GenC can be cleared with aptitude and communication; coding needed for Next/Pro.

mech_civil.note: Typically eligible for GenC as engineering graduates (confirm in notice). Focus on aptitude, English and basic programming/SQL.

all.note: Secondary sources commonly cite 60% or 6.0 CGPA (some drives differ), no active backlogs, and for GenC Next an overall gap of at most 2 years. Cognizant's official GenC page currently lists Analyst Trainee openings for 2024–2026 batches with a three-year degree; engineering-track rules come from your drive notice.

jd_skills.note: Verbal section with a reportedly strict sectional cutoff.
One programming language for the coding assessment (any common language).
Secondary sources say certifications are considered when placing candidates into higher tracks.
Helpful for interviews; not a stated requirement.

hr_focus: Flexibility on job location and shifts.
Why Cognizant, and which GenC track you are aiming for.
